Thanks for the demo last week. Before we finalize the DPA redlines, our security team needs clarification on how Redwood handles deletions that surface in backups and replicated logs. Specifically:

- If a user requests erasure under our DSR, how long until associated logs and snapshots are removed from backups?
- Do you support an expedited/accelerated backup purge for customers who need a faster removal window (we'd expect supporting attestation)?
- Any carveouts for forensic holds or legal holds that would delay purges?

Hi Ryan —

Thanks for the clear questions and the data map. High-level answers below; I also sketched a pragmatic option tailored to Starlite’s DPA needs.

On your points:

1) Standard deletion workflow and timelines
   - User-initiated erasure: immediate logical delete (metadata flag) at T0.
   - Primary store purge: background job removes object content within 30 days (default async window to avoid race conditions).
   - Snapshot/backups: full backup retention is 90 days by default; point-in-time snapshots are retained for 180 days.
   - Audit/log copies: operational logs are retained in hot storage for 30 days, then moved to immutable cold storage for 180 days unless scoped by the customer.

2) Expedited backup purge (accelerated purge)
   - We do support a customer-requested accelerated purge process. Steps: customer request + legal attestation -> ops review -> expedited purge job targeting account-specific snapshots and backup segments.
   - Typical SLA for expedited purge: 14–30 days depending on the age and distribution of snapshots across subprocessors/cloud regions. Very large accounts or cross-region backups can push to 45 days.

3) Forensic/legal holds
   - Legal holds override scheduled purges. When a hold is in place, we preserve the relevant objects/snapshots and mark them as in-scope for retention. We provide an audit log of hold application and removal.

Proposal for Starlite (practical option)

- Default model: keep Redwood defaults (primary 30d, backups 90d, snapshots 180d).
- Starlite-specific commitment (optional addendum): a 60-day account-targeted backup purge timeline for DSR-driven deletions with a documented attestation from Starlite legal. This reduces the exposure window while remaining operable for our infra team.
- Exceptions: any legal/forensic hold must be raised to legal@starlitehealth.com and will suspend purge for the specified assets.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll attach our deletion runbook excerpt and a proposed purge schedule so you can share with legal/procurement.
- If Starlite wants the 60-day addendum, procurement/legal needs to sign a one-paragraph schedule amendment; we can route via DocuSign.

For transparency, I’ve attached: redwood_deletion_runbook.pdf and a proposed-purge-schedule.xlsx.

If helpful, we can schedule a short call with Marcus (ops) to walk the purge steps and recovery risks.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Hey team —

Quick ops confirmation and a few nitty-gritty points on the proposed 60-day targeted backup purge: 

1) Feasibility
   - We can run an account-scoped purge that targets incremental backups and snapshots created after the deletion event. For most accounts this completes within 14–30 days.
   - If backups are replicated to multiple cloud regions/subprocessors, we escalate to a 30–45d window — cross-region snapshots require coordinated subprocessor deletion acknowledgements.

2) Risk and restore window
   - Accelerated purge increases the chance that a customer-initiated restore (within the old 90-day window) will be impossible for purged segments. We’ll provide a restore-risk advisory in the attestation package.

3) Technical note on logs
   - Operational logs live in two places: a) hot logging for 30d, b) immutable cold archives for 180d. The expedited purge will mark affected log segments for deletion in cold archives and raise a subprocessor work order. Cold archive purges are batched weekly.

Operational steps (summary):
- Legal attestation received -> create Purge Ticket (PURL) -> lock account snapshot exports -> run dry-run to identify object IDs -> schedule account-scoped purge job -> confirm subprocessor ACKs -> final audit delivered to customer.

Attachments: backup_schedule.xlsx (ops schedule snippet)
